title: Parsing the Epstein Files for JMail — Palak Agarwal & Omar Alhait, Reducto
talk_summary: A Reducto developer-relations lead and founding engineer describe how Reducto's agentic OCR/document-extraction platform parsed 3M+ pages of Epstein files to power JMail, emphasizing schema-driven extraction, a studio for iterating configs, and custom benchmarks. The talk is mostly product demo and Q&A; the transferable mechanisms are eval-by-schema, parse-then-extract pipelines, and citation/entity post-processing.

takeaways.technique: Vibe-eval then scale to a systematic benchmark set
takeaways.what_they_do: They start by eyeballing outputs in a studio on a few documents, then move to 100-1000 document systematic evals, and note every customer must build their own benchmark because public ones don't reflect their config.
takeaways.evidence_quote: gather a simple data set you can do some like vibe eval just look look in studio see if the outputs make sense and then like as you want to scale it out then get like 100 documents a thousand documents do something more systematic

takeaways.what_they_do: They separate a parse stage (structure/layout) from downstream extraction stages, so each stage gets clean structured input rather than raw messy documents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what we're actually doing in like extraction is taking the parse results and then feeding them into, you know, some extraction pipeline downstream

takeaways.technique: Separate citation/attribution model from extraction model
takeaways.what_they_do: One model extracts data, a second model determines where each extracted piece came from (citation), plus post-processing to link entities.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have like a citation model, right? Where we know we have, you know, one model that could be responsible for extraction ... another model that's also responsible for once this data is extracted, where is each piece kind of extracted from

takeaways.technique: Schema/config as the primary tuning surface
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat the extraction schema and per-stage prompts/configs as the main lever, iterating in a studio and redeploying the same pipeline; enhanced schema generation tailors the schema to actual document content.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your extract schema is sort of like the paintbrush on your reductto canvas ... it definitely drives everything that you um you know, you get out of the schema

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of a single pass committing to an answer, the model flags uncertain regions, corrects them, then proceeds to the next step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: rather than making a single pass and committing to an answer the model flags things that it's uncertain about corrects them and then moves on to the next step

takeaways.what_they_do: Bulk parsing stressed their own infra and a colleague had to ask them to slow down, illustrating that batch jobs need explicit backpressure against shared capacity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we put a, you know, a decent amount of stress on our infra. And so, Alvin was sending me a lot of fun messages late at night like, "Hey, bro, can you slow down?"
